title: How to Become a Confident English Speaker
speaker: Tom Wilkinson

keywords.def: A belief in your ability to do something successfully or deal with challenges effectively.
A lack of confidence in your own abilities, decisions, or skills.
A person’s belief that they can successfully complete a specific task or achieve a particular goal.
To deal with a problem, challenge, or difficult circumstance successfully.
More advanced, complex, or developed than something simpler.
To deal successfully with a difficult situation or challenge.
The state of not knowing exactly what will happen in the future.

sentences.en: What is confidence? What does a confident English speaker look like?
sentences.zh: 什么是自信？一个自信的英语说者是什么样的？

sentences.en: And how can you become a confident speaker?
sentences.zh: 你又该如何成为一个自信的英语说者呢？

sentences.en: This episode is going to try and answer some of these important questions.
sentences.zh: 本期节目将尝试解答其中一些重要的问题。

sentences.en: You might assume that someone with perfect grammar, a huge vocabulary, and a native-like accent will be a confident speaker.
sentences.zh: 你可能会认为，那些语法完美、词汇量巨大且带有母语般口音的人一定是个自信的英语说者。

sentences.en: But that is not necessarily the case. Over the years, I’ve met English learners with excellent English, but who were afraid to speak.
sentences.zh: 但事实并非如此。这些年来，我遇到过许多英语水平极佳，却害怕开口的英语学习者。

sentences.en: And learners with much weaker English ability, but who seemed completely confident and comfortable communicating.
sentences.zh: 还有一些英语能力明显较弱的学习者，却显得极其自信，沟通起来游刃有余。

sentences.en: This suggests that confidence and language ability are not exactly the same thing.
sentences.zh: 这表明自信和语言能力并不完全是一回事。

sentences.en: So I want to explore confidence from a slightly more psychological perspective.
sentences.zh: 因此，我想从一个稍微偏向心理学的视角来探讨自信。

sentences.en: What is confidence? What is the opposite of confidence?
sentences.zh: 什么是自信？自信的反义词是什么？

sentences.en: Why is confidence so important for language learners?
sentences.zh: 为什么自信对语言学习者如此重要？

sentences.en: How about self-efficacy? And how can you become a more confident English speaker?
sentences.zh: 那什么是自我效能感呢？你又该如何成为一个更自信的英语说者？

sentences.en: According to the Cambridge Dictionary, the definition of confident is “being certain of your abilities or having trust in people, plans, or the future.”
sentences.zh: 根据剑桥词典的定义，自信的定义是“对自己的能力确信不疑，或者对人、计划或未来充满信任”。

sentences.en: I think this might be a little bit different to what many of you listening assume confidence means, especially what confidence means in practice.
sentences.zh: 我认为这可能和你听众中许多人以为的自信有点不同，尤其是自信在实践中的含义。

sentences.en: Many people think confidence means being fearless.
sentences.zh: 许多人认为自信意味着无所畏惧。

sentences.en: You see a confident person as someone who doesn’t feel nervous or doesn’t really make mistakes.
sentences.zh: 你把自信的人看作是那种不会感到紧张、或者基本上不会犯错的人。

sentences.en: But being certain of your abilities and trusting your skills is not the same thing as being perfect and fearless.
sentences.zh: 但确信自己的能力并信任自己的技能，并不等于完美无缺和无所畏惧。

sentences.en: Confidence is sometimes understood as a belief in your ability to handle a situation successfully.
sentences.zh: 自信有时被理解为一种相信自己能够成功应对某种局面的信念。

sentences.en: That definition doesn’t say anything about “being perfect.” Instead, it means that you trust yourself to deal with challenges when they appear.
sentences.zh: 这个定义并没有提到“完美无缺”。相反，这意味着当你面对挑战时，你相信自己能够应对。

sentences.en: For example, think about a professional footballer.
sentences.zh: 比如，想想职业足球运动员。

sentences.en: The World Cup is on right now, so think about a professional footballer in the World Cup playing for one of the world’s top teams.
sentences.zh: 世界杯现在正在进行，所以想想正在世界杯赛场上为世界顶级球队之一效力的职业足球运动员。

sentences.en: They are almost certainly a confident footballer because it is difficult, maybe impossible, to get to the top level, to be playing for your country, without trusting in your ability.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎肯定是自信的足球运动员，因为如果不相信自己的能力，要达到顶级水平、为国出战是很难的，甚至是不可想象的。

sentences.en: But even if they are confident, I’m sure they still make mistakes, like giving the ball away or getting a red card.
sentences.zh: 但即使他们很自信，我敢肯定他们仍然会犯错，比如传丢球或吃红牌。

sentences.en: And I’m sure they still get nervous before games.
sentences.zh: 而且我敢肯定他们在比赛前依然会感到紧张。

sentences.en: The same idea applies to language learning, English learning.
sentences.zh: 同样的道理也适用于语言学习，也就是英语学习。

sentences.en: We’ll talk about this more later in the episode, but I think a confident English speaker is someone who trusts their ability to communicate even when things don’t go perfectly.
sentences.zh: 我们在节目后面会更详细地讨论这一点，但我认为一个自信的英语说者是这样一个人：即使事情进展得不那么完美，他们也相信自己有能力进行沟通。

sentences.en: Having a great knowledge of grammar and vocabulary doesn’t necessarily mean you will be confident.
sentences.zh: 拥有丰富的语法和词汇知识并不一定意味着你就会自信。

sentences.en: Confidence is connected to the idea of uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 自信与“不确定性”这个概念息息相关。

sentences.en: It’s the opposite of certain. Uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 它是“确定”的反义词。不确定性。

sentences.en: When you start a new job, or you travel to a new country, or you do something different from your regular schedule, you will be surrounded by uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 当你开始一份新工作，或者去一个新国家旅游，或者做一些打破常规的事情时，你身边将充满不确定性。

sentences.en: You cannot predict every challenge you will face.
sentences.zh: 你无法预测自己将面临的每一个挑战。

sentences.en: Confidence is what allows you, allows us all, to carry on despite uncertainty.
sentences.zh: 正是自信让我们——让我们所有人——能够在面对不确定性时继续前行。

sentences.en: Confidence is the trust that you will be able to cope if anything goes wrong.
sentences.zh: 自信就是坚信如果出了什么差错，自己也能够应付。

sentences.en: This idea is important because a lot of people misunderstand confidence.
sentences.zh: 这个概念很重要，因为很多人对自信有误解。

sentences.en: They think confidence means that you believe nothing will go wrong, nothing bad will happen.
sentences.zh: 他们以为自信意味着你坚信什么都不会出差错，什么坏事都不会发生。

sentences.en: But actually, I think it’s a bit different.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，我觉得它有点不同。

sentences.en: If you’re confident, you believe that if something bad happens, you can manage it.
sentences.zh: 如果你很自信，你就会相信即使有坏事发生，你也能应付得了。

sentences.en: You have the skills, you have the ability, you have the knowledge, you have the experience, you have… You trust yourself to deal with difficult situations.
sentences.zh: 你有技能、有能力、有知识、有经验，你有……你相信自己能够处理困难局面。

sentences.en: So confidence is not the same as ability.
sentences.zh: 所以自信不等于能力。

sentences.en: Ability is your actual skill level. Confidence is your belief in your ability.
sentences.zh: 能力是你实际的技能水平。自信则是你对自身能力的信念。

sentences.en: It might be easier to understand confidence by considering it in the negative.
sentences.zh: 通过从反面来思考，或许更容易理解自信。

sentences.en: What is the opposite of confidence? You might have answered low ability or lack of skill.
sentences.zh: 自信的反义词是什么？你可能会回答能力低下或缺乏技能。

sentences.en: But as I said, confidence and ability are not the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但正如我所说，自信和能力并不是一回事。

sentences.en: Think about someone who has studied English for 10 years, maybe some of you listening.
sentences.zh: 想想某个学了十年英语的人，也许在座的各位就有人这样。

sentences.en: You have a large vocabulary. You understand complex grammar.
sentences.zh: 你词汇量很大。你懂复杂的语法。

sentences.en: You read difficult articles. You listen to Thinking in English episodes.
sentences.zh: 你阅读高难度的文章。你收听《Thinking in English》播客。

sentences.en: But maybe you avoid speaking whenever possible because you are afraid of making mistakes.
sentences.zh: 但只要有可能，你可能就会避免开口说话，因为你害怕犯错。

sentences.en: Clearly, you have a lot of ability. Your problem is a lack of confidence.
sentences.zh: 显然，你很有能力。你的问题是缺乏自信。

sentences.en: I think the opposite of confidence is self-doubt.
sentences.zh: 我认为自信的反义词是自我怀疑。

sentences.en: Self-doubt is uncertainty about your own abilities.
sentences.zh: 自我怀疑是对自身能力的不确定。

sentences.en: It is the feeling that you’re not good enough, you’re not intelligent enough, you’re not skilled enough to handle a situation.
sentences.zh: 那是这样一种感觉：觉得自己不够优秀、不够聪明、技能不够，无法应付某种局面。

sentences.en: You doubt yourself. Everyone experiences self-doubt.
sentences.zh: 你怀疑自己。每个人都会经历自我怀疑。

sentences.en: I think it’s a normal part of being human and probably a useful part of being human.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是人之常情，可能也是人类生存中一个有用部分。

sentences.en: But self-doubt can become so strong that it stops us using our skills and our abilities.
sentences.zh: 但自我怀疑有时会变得如此强烈，以至于阻碍我们使用自己的技能和能力。

sentences.en: Think about if you were to go out into the streets of London and try and have a conversation with someone.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，如果你走到伦敦街头，试着跟某人搭话。

sentences.en: Do you think that you could successfully have a conversation in English with a random stranger?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你能用英语和一个陌生人成功对话吗？

sentences.en: Or do you think you can’t do that? If you lack confidence, you probably answered negatively.
sentences.zh: 还是说你觉得你做不到？如果你缺乏自信，你的回答很可能是否定的。

sentences.en: You probably said, “Oh, I could not have a conversation,” when I’m almost sure all of you can have a conversation in English because you’re listening to this podcast.
sentences.zh: 你可能会说，“哦，我没法跟人对话”，但我几乎可以确信在座的各位都能用英语对话，因为你们正在听这个播客。

sentences.en: A language learner, like you learning English or like myself learning Japanese, who suffers with self-doubt, could choose the safest option.
sentences.zh: 一个英语学习者——就像正在学英语的你，或是像正在学日语的我——如果饱受自我怀疑的困扰，可能会选择最稳妥的选项。

sentences.en: And the safest option is to avoid speaking.
sentences.zh: 而最稳妥的选项就是避免开口说话。

sentences.en: If you don’t speak, you can’t embarrass yourself.
sentences.zh: 如果你不说话，就不会出丑。

sentences.en: If you don’t speak, nothing can go wrong.
sentences.zh: 如果你不说话，就不会出任何岔子。

sentences.en: Psychologists sometimes call this “avoidance behavior “.
sentences.zh: 心理学家有时称之为“回避行为”。

sentences.en: Avoidance behavior is when people stay away from situations that make them uncomfortable or anxious.
sentences.zh: 回避行为是指人们远离那些让他们感到不舒服或焦虑的情境。

sentences.en: You avoid the things that make you anxious.
sentences.zh: 你避开那些让你焦虑的事情。

sentences.en: This is okay for you because it makes you feel relieved.
sentences.zh: 这对你来说挺好，因为这能让你感到解脱。

sentences.en: You don’t need to do something out of your comfort zone.
sentences.zh: 你不需要去做任何走出舒适区的事。

sentences.en: You don’t need to be embarrassed or feel anxious or feel uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 你不需要出丑、感到焦虑或浑身不自在。

sentences.en: But you do lose an opportunity. You lose an opportunity to get some more experience.
sentences.zh: 但你确实失去了一个机会。你失去了一个获取更多经验的机会。

sentences.en: Confident people still feel nervous, of course.
sentences.zh: 当然，自信的人依然会感到紧张。

sentences.en: A confident public speaker still feels anxious before giving a presentation.
sentences.zh: 一个自信的公众演讲者在做演讲前依然会感到焦虑。

sentences.en: A confident athlete still feels pressure before running in the Olympic 100-meter race.
sentences.zh: 一个自信的运动员在参加奥运会百米赛跑前依然会感受到压力。

sentences.en: All of those athletes in the World Cup final are confident in their ability, but they’re probably nervous.
sentences.zh: 世界杯决赛场上的所有那些运动员都对自己的能力充满自信，但他们很可能也很紧张。

sentences.en: And a confident language learner still feels nervous before speaking with a native speaker.
sentences.zh: 而一个自信的语言学习者在与母语者对话前依然会感到紧张。

sentences.en: I do. I feel nervous whenever I have to use Japanese.
sentences.zh: 我就是这样。每当我必须使用日语时，我都觉得紧张。

sentences.en: The difference, I guess though, is that confident people don’t allow the fear to stop them.
sentences.zh: 不过我想区别在于，自信的人不会让恐惧阻止他们前进。

sentences.en: Humans are constantly in situations where we don’t have complete information.
sentences.zh: 人类常常处于无法掌握全部信息的境地中。

sentences.en: Every day, we make decisions without knowing exactly what will happen.
sentences.zh: 每一天，我们在不知晓具体结果的情况下做决定。

sentences.en: Where the outcome is not a hundred percent certain.
sentences.zh: 结果并不是百分之百确定的。

sentences.en: From an evolutionary perspective, this is why confidence has been so valuable.
sentences.zh: 从进化的角度来看，这就是为什么自信如此宝贵。

sentences.en: The word evolutionary refers to the long process through which species change and adapt over many generations.
sentences.zh: “进化”一词指的是物种在许多代中发生变化和适应的漫长过程。

sentences.en: Human beings evolved in environments that were unpredictable, so our ancestors faced uncertainty all the time.
sentences.zh: 人类进化于不可预测的环境中，因此我们的祖先时刻面对着不确定性。

sentences.en: Where would they get their food? Could they find a cave to sleep in today?
sentences.zh: 他们的食物从哪来？今天能不能找到一个山洞睡觉？

sentences.en: Was it going to rain? Was it going to be sunny?
sentences.zh: 会下雨吗？会是个晴天吗？

sentences.en: Was it going to snow? As a result, humans have developed mechanisms, psychological tools, that help us function in uncertain situations.
sentences.zh: 会下雪吗？因此，人类进化出了一些机制，也就是心理工具，帮助我们在不确定的环境中运转。

sentences.en: And confidence is a great example of a psychological mechanism that helps us deal with uncertain situations.
sentences.zh: 而自信就是心理机制的一个绝佳例子，它能帮我们应对不确定的局势。

sentences.en: Of course, confidence can sometimes be excessive.
sentences.zh: 当然，自信有时也可能过头。

sentences.en: Someone who believes they cannot fail might take unnecessary risks.
sentences.zh: 一个坚信自己不会失败的人可能会去冒不必要的风险。

sentences.en: So that’s why we need to distinguish between “confidence” and “overconfidence.” Overconfidence is when someone’s belief in their ability is higher than their actual ability.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们需要区分“自信”与“过度自信”。过度自信是指一个人对自己能力的信念高于其实际能力。

sentences.en: You have too much confidence in yourself.
sentences.zh: 你对自己太有自信了。

sentences.en: I have spoken to hundreds, maybe even thousands, of English learners over the past decade.
sentences.zh: 在过去的十年里，我和成百上千、甚至可能上万名英语学习者交谈过。

sentences.en: I worked with children in schools. I taught online English classes to adults for a few years.
sentences.zh: 我在学校里和孩子们一起工作。我教过几年成人在线英语课。

sentences.en: I’ve been running the Thinking in English Conversation Club since 2022.
sentences.zh: 我从2022年开始运营《Thinking in English》英语角俱乐部。

sentences.en: And to be honest, it’s clear when someone is confident.
sentences.zh: 老实说，一个人是否自信是很明显的。

sentences.en: I think sometimes people mistake a confident English speaker for someone who is highly proficient.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有时人们会把自信的英语说者误认为精通英语的人。

sentences.en: Proficient means skilled or capable at doing something.
sentences.zh: “精通”指的是在某事上熟练或能干。

sentences.en: These things are definitely related. Proficiency and confidence are related, but they’re not the same thing.
sentences.zh: 这些事情绝对是相关的。熟练度和自信相关，但它们不是一回事。

sentences.en: Improving your English can increase your confidence, but confidence is not necessarily the result of improving your English.
sentences.zh: 提高英语水平可以增强你的自信，但自信并不一定就是提高英语水平的结果。

sentences.en: You can be confident without being a high-level speaker.
sentences.zh: 你不需要成为高级水平的说话者就能做到自信。

sentences.en: I like to think about myself here. I speak Japanese to a decent level, my listening is pretty good, and I use Japanese every day in my life.
sentences.zh: 这里我想拿自己举个例子。我的日语达到了不错的水平，我的听力相当好，而且我每天的生活中都在使用日语。

sentences.en: But I’m not that technically skilled. I haven’t passed the highest level of the Japanese proficiency test.
sentences.zh: 但我的技术并不那么熟练。我没有通过日语能力测试的最高级别。

sentences.en: I often make grammar mistakes or vocabulary errors.
sentences.zh: 我经常犯语法错误或词汇错误。

sentences.en: I’m not particularly good at reading. I’m trying to improve my overall level.
sentences.zh: 我的阅读特别不在行。我正在努力提升我的整体水平。

sentences.en: But one thing that is true is I’m a pretty confident speaker.
sentences.zh: 但有一点是真的，我是一个相当自信的说话者。

sentences.en: I will speak to people often. I’ll speak to anyone, and I’ll speak in various different situations and about various different matters.
sentences.zh: 我经常和人说话。我会和任何人交流，而且我会在各种不同的情境下、谈论各种不同的事情。

sentences.en: I’m not the best speaker. Like I said, I make a lot of mistakes, but because I’m quite confident, I can communicate my point.
sentences.zh: 我不是最好的说话者。正如我所说，我犯了很多错误，但因为我相当自信，所以我能够表达我的观点。

sentences.en: Not as efficiently, but I can do it effectively.
sentences.zh: 虽然表达得没那么高效，但我能做到有效沟通。

sentences.en: I have friends who are much better technically at Japanese than I am.
sentences.zh: 我有些朋友，他们的日语技术比我好得多。

sentences.en: They can read more, understand more, they know more grammar.
sentences.zh: 他们读得更多、懂的更多，他们知道更多语法。

sentences.en: They are perfectly comfortable with business Japanese or academic Japanese when they’re reading or when they’re writing or when they’re listening, but they’re not confident speakers.
sentences.zh: 他们在阅读、写作或听力时，对商务日语或学术日语游刃有余，但他们并不是自信的说话者。

sentences.en: They do things like apologizing for their language level or hesitating before every sentence.
sentences.zh: 他们会做一些诸如为自己的语言水平道歉，或者在每个句子前犹豫不决的事情。

sentences.en: When I speak, I try to speak freely. I like to get involved in conversations.
sentences.zh: 当我说话时，我尽量畅所欲言。我喜欢参与对话。

sentences.en: I like to ask questions. I’m quite comfortable communicating.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢提问。我交流起来相当自在。

sentences.en: I make a lot of mistakes, but I don’t let that interrupt my conversations.
sentences.zh: 我犯了很多错误，但我不会让错误打断我的对话。

sentences.en: My less confident, technically better at Japanese friends sometimes speak a bit less freely.
sentences.zh: 我那些日语技术更好、但没那么自信的朋友，有时说话就没那么自由。

sentences.en: So confidence is often visible through your behavior rather than your language ability.
sentences.zh: 所以，与其说自信体现在语言能力上，倒不如说它往往是通过你的行为表现出来的。

sentences.en: Confidence is about how you act, and especially how you act when you do not know something or you make a mistake.
sentences.zh: 自信关乎你的行事方式，尤其是当你不知道某事或犯了错时的行事方式。

sentences.en: A confident English speaker finds a way to express their ideas when they don’t know the correct word.
sentences.zh: 一个自信的英语说者在不知道正确的词时，总能找到方法表达自己的想法。

sentences.en: A less confident speaker might freeze or stop speaking when in the same situation.
sentences.zh: 而不太自信的说话者在遇到同样情况时，可能会僵住或停止说话。

sentences.en: One characteristic of a confident English speaker is that they prioritize communication over perfection.
sentences.zh: 自信的英语说者有一个特点，那就是他们把沟通看得比完美更重要。

sentences.en: So prioritize means to treat something as more important than something else.
sentences.zh: 所以“优先考虑”指的是把某事看得比其他事更重要。

sentences.en: If your goal is to be perfect, it’s going to make it harder for you to communicate.
sentences.zh: 如果你的目标是做到完美，这会让你更难进行沟通。

sentences.en: Imagine you’re trying to tell someone about a trip you went on this weekend.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，你正试图向某人讲述你这个周末去旅行的经历。

sentences.en: If you are perfection-focused in your language learning you might spend a few seconds worrying about grammar before you’re speaking, and then you repeatedly hesitate when you’re unsure of a word.
sentences.zh: 如果你的语言学习追求完美主义，你可能在开口前花几秒钟担心语法，接着在不确定某个词时反复犹豫。

sentences.en: But someone who just cares about communicating might just simply tell the story without really caring about any mistakes, and they’re likely to be a bit more fluent.
sentences.zh: 但一个只关心沟通的人可能会直接把故事讲出来，根本不在乎什么错误，而且他们往往会流利一些。

sentences.en: I believe that confidence is one of the most important factors in successful language learning.
sentences.zh: 我相信自信是成功语言学习中最核心的因素之一。

sentences.en: Confidence influences your behavior, and your behavior influences your progress.
sentences.zh: 自信会影响你的行为，而你的行为会影响你的进步。

sentences.en: Let’s think about two hypothetical English learners.
sentences.zh: 让我们设想两位假设中的英语学习者。

sentences.en: Both learners have the exact same level of English.
sentences.zh: 这两位学习者的英语水平完全相同。

sentences.en: They know the same vocabulary and the same grammar.
sentences.zh: 他们掌握着相同的词汇和相同的语法。

sentences.en: They have achieved similar scores on English tests.
sentences.zh: 他们在英语测试中取得了相似的分数。

sentences.en: But one learner is confident and the other is not.
sentences.zh: 但其中一个学习者很自信，另一个则不然。

sentences.en: The confident learner volunteers during lessons, and they like to start conversations with random people in English.
sentences.zh: 自信的学习者在课堂上积极发言，他们喜欢用英语和陌生人搭讪。

sentences.en: If they don’t know something, they like to ask questions.
sentences.zh: 如果他们有什么不懂的，他们喜欢提问。

sentences.en: They participate in the Thinking in English conversation clubs on Tuesdays and Wednesdays.
sentences.zh: 他们参加周二和周三的《Thinking in English》英语角俱乐部。

sentences.en: Or they go online and leave comments on YouTube videos or blog articles.
sentences.zh: 或者他们上网在YouTube视频或博客文章下留言。

sentences.en: They write social media posts in English.
sentences.zh: 他们用英语写社交媒体帖子。

sentences.en: They use English all the time. The unconfident learner avoids speaking whenever possible.
sentences.zh: 他们无时无刻不在使用英语。不自信的学习者只要有机会就会避免开口。

sentences.en: They hesitate before answering questions.
sentences.zh: 他们在回答问题前犹豫不决。

sentences.en: They worry about making mistakes. They wait to use English until they feel ready.
sentences.zh: 他们担心犯错。他们要等到自己觉得准备好了才肯使用英语。

sentences.en: Which learner is likely to improve more over the long term?
sentences.zh: 哪个学习者从长远来看更有可能取得进步？

sentences.en: It’s almost certainly the confident learner because they gave themselves so many more opportunities to use English.
sentences.zh: 几乎可以肯定是那个自信的学习者，因为他们给了自己更多使用英语的机会。

sentences.en: Languages are a skill, and skills develop through practice.
sentences.zh: 语言是一种技能，而技能是通过练习发展起来的。

sentences.en: Eventually, you need to speak, to learn how to speak.
sentences.zh: 最终，你需要开口说，才能学会如何说。

sentences.en: Confidence gives you more chances. It’s a kind of positive feedback loop.
sentences.zh: 自信为你争取到更多机会。这是一种正向反馈循环。

sentences.en: A feedback loop is where the outcome influences the thing it created.
sentences.zh: 反馈循环是指结果反过来影响创造该结果的事物。

sentences.en: That’s a bit confusing, but… confidence leads to speaking, speaking leads to experience, experience leads to improvement, improvement leads to more confidence, and the cycle repeats.
sentences.zh: 这听起来有点让人糊涂，但是……自信带来开口，开口带来经验，经验带来进步，进步带来更多的自信，然后这个循环不断重复。

sentences.en: There’s also a negative version of this loop.
sentences.zh: 这个循环也有负面版本。

sentences.en: A learner lacks confidence. Because they lack confidence, they avoid speaking.
sentences.zh: 一个学习者缺乏自信。因为缺乏自信，他们就避免开口。

sentences.en: Because they avoid speaking, they gain less experience.
sentences.zh: 因为避免开口，他们获得的经验就变少。

sentences.en: Because they gain less experience, their progress is slow.
sentences.zh: 因为获得的经验少，他们的进步就很慢。

sentences.en: And because their progress is slow, they become even less confident.
sentences.zh: 而因为进步缓慢，他们变得更加缺乏自信。

sentences.en: Again, the cycle repeats. So many people are scared to speak in English, right?
sentences.zh: 同样，这个循环不断重复。很多人害怕说英语，对吧？

sentences.en: But if you join something like my conversation club, or if you don’t want to join mine, there’s many other conversation clubs online.
sentences.zh: 但如果你加入类似我的英语角俱乐部，或者如果你不想加入我的，网上还有很多其他的英语角俱乐部。

sentences.en: There are apps like HelloTalk or language learning sites like italki or something, where you can go and you can have conversations in English.
sentences.zh: 还有像HelloTalk这样的应用，或者是italki之类的语言学习网站，你可以在上面用英语进行交流。

sentences.en: Finding a safe space, a place with other learners, a place with people who are in the same situation as you, I think is important because it’s safe.
sentences.zh: 找到一个安全的空间，一个有其他学习者的空间，一个有和你处境相同的人的空间，我认为这很重要，因为它是安全的。

sentences.en: It gives you a safe place to speak in English, and that will increase your confidence.
sentences.zh: 它为你提供了一个安全的英语口语环境，这会增强你的自信。

sentences.en: And then when your confidence is high enough, you can go out in the real world.
sentences.zh: 然后，当你的自信心足够高时，你就可以走向现实世界了。

sentences.en: Sometimes people tell me they want to wait until their grammar or vocabulary is better, and then they’re going to start speaking.
sentences.zh: 有时候人们告诉我，他们想等到自己的语法或词汇更好时再开始说英语。

sentences.en: But there is always more grammar to learn, always more vocabulary to learn.
sentences.zh: 但永远都有更多的语法要学，永远都有更多的词汇要学。

sentences.en: When I started learning Japanese, I was speaking in Japanese to Japanese people within the first week of studying the language.
sentences.zh: 当我开始学日语时，我在学习语言的第一周内就开始和日本人用日语交谈了。

sentences.en: Now, I was lucky because I lived in Japan at the time.
sentences.zh: 当然，我很幸运，因为我当时住在日本。

sentences.en: I started learning Japanese on the day I moved to Japan, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我搬到日本的那天就开始学日语了。

sentences.en: And I improved really quickly. You probably won’t have that situation where you move to a new country and start learning their language, but you can apply that principle, right?
sentences.zh: 而且我进步得非常快。你可能不会遇到那种搬到一个新国家并开始学习当地语言的情况，但你可以运用这个原则，对吧？

sentences.en: Speak now. You don’t have to wait until you’re better.
sentences.zh: 现在就说。你不需要等到变得更好再开口。

sentences.en: Start speaking. Confidence and ability seem like they should go in the same direction, but it’s not always the case.
sentences.zh: 开始说吧。自信和能力看起来似乎应该朝着同一个方向发展，但事实并非总是如此。

sentences.en: Sometimes we might see English improving, but confidence stagnating or decreasing.
sentences.zh: 有时我们可能会看到英语水平在提高，但自信心却停滞不前或在下降。

sentences.en: It sounds strange, but it is common. Some advanced learners are less confident than when they were beginners.
sentences.zh: 听起来很奇怪，但这很常见。有些高级学习者反而没有他们刚入门时那么自信。

sentences.en: I’ve experienced this. I probably felt less embarrassed, less anxious about using my Japanese eight years ago when I was a beginner The reason is… when I started to learn Japanese, my understanding of the language was so limited.
sentences.zh: 我深有体会。八年前我刚开始学日语时，使用日语时感到的尴尬和焦虑可能反而没那么多。原因在于……当我刚开始学日语时，我对这门语言的了解极其有限。

sentences.en: I didn’t know grammar or vocabulary or idioms, pronunciation.
sentences.zh: 我不知道语法、词汇或习语、发音。

sentences.en: I didn’t know accents, cultural references, Japanese communication styles.
sentences.zh: 我不知道口音、文化背景、日语的沟通风格。

sentences.en: I didn’t know any of that stuff. I was unaware of how much there was to learn because my knowledge was so limited.
sentences.zh: 我什么都不知道。由于知识极其有限，我根本不知道还有那么多东西要学。

sentences.en: And that meant I felt quite confident, surprisingly confident.
sentences.zh: 这意味着我感到相当自信，出奇地自信。

sentences.en: I knew enough to order food. I knew enough to introduce myself well.
sentences.zh: 我知道的足够用来点餐。我知道的足够用来好好做个自我介绍。

sentences.en: I could have simple conversations. I did not see the complexity of the language, so I assumed I was doing well.
sentences.zh: 我能进行简单的对话。我没有看出这门语言的复杂性，所以我以为自己干得不错。

sentences.en: “Look at me, I’m having conversations.” But as my Japanese improved, I began noticing things.
sentences.zh: “看我，我都能对话了。”但随着我的日语水平提高，我开始注意到一些事情。

sentences.en: I began noticing that my ability was not as good as I thought.
sentences.zh: 我开始注意到我的能力其实没有想象中那么好。

sentences.en: I realized there were multiple ways to express the same idea in Japanese.
sentences.zh: 我意识到日语中表达同一个意思有多种不同的方式。

sentences.en: I noticed that there are 10 similar words which mean the same thing.
sentences.zh: 我注意到有10个意思相同的类似词汇。

sentences.en: I noticed I was making mistakes. Quite often, I speak, and I know my grammar is wrong, but I don’t know how to fix it, and it gets frustrating.
sentences.zh: 我注意到我在犯错。很多时候，我开口说话时明知语法是错的，却又不知道该怎么修正，这让人感到沮丧。

sentences.en: This increased awareness, the awareness that you are not as good as you think you are, makes you feel less confident.
sentences.zh: 这种意识的增强——也就是意识到自己并没有想象中那么好——会让你觉得没那么自信了。

sentences.en: This is related to the, oh, the Dunning-Kruger effect.
sentences.zh: 这与那个，哦，达克效应有关。

sentences.en: You might have seen it on the internet. It’s quite a popular thing.
sentences.zh: 你可能在网上看过。这是个相当火的现象。

sentences.en: It’s a graph that shows levels of ability and confidence.
sentences.zh: 这是一张展示能力水平与自信水平的图表。

sentences.en: You can find lots of information about the Dunning-Kruger Effect out there, so I won’t explain it here.
sentences.zh: 你可以在网上找到很多关于达克效应的信息，所以我在这里就不解释了。

sentences.en: But one of the things you notice when you look at the graph is that experts, the people with the most knowledge about something, tend to maybe not be as confident as people with less knowledge.
sentences.zh: 但当你观察这张图表时，你会注意到的一点是：专家，也就是对某事了解最多的人，可能往往不如那些懂得较少的人自信。

sentences.en: Often people with limited knowledge of something can be more confident.
sentences.zh: 通常，对某事了解有限的人反而会更自信。

sentences.en: So how can you become more confident? Personality plays a role in this.
sentences.zh: 那么你该如何变得更自信呢？性格在其中发挥了一定作用。

sentences.en: Some people are naturally more outgoing, naturally more comfortable taking risks than other people.
sentences.zh: 有些人天生更外向，天生比其他人更乐意冒风险。

sentences.en: But a lot of confidence is learned. One of the most influential psychologists to study this topic was Albert Bandura.
sentences.zh: 但很大一部分自信是后天习得的。研究这一课题最有影响力的心理学家之一是阿尔伯特·班杜拉。

sentences.en: Bandura introduced the concept of self-efficacy, or the theory of self-efficacy.
sentences.zh: 班杜拉引入了自我效能的概念，或者说自我效能理论。

sentences.en: Self-efficacy is very similar to confidence, but it’s slightly different.
sentences.zh: 自我效能与自信非常相似，但略有不同。

sentences.en: It refers to a person’s belief in their ability to perform a specific task or achieve a particular goal.
sentences.zh: 它指的是一个人对自己有能力执行特定任务或实现特定目标的信念。

sentences.en: Confidence is your overall feeling. You’re confident.
sentences.zh: 自信是你的总体感觉。你很自信。

sentences.en: Self-efficacy is your specific belief in your ability for a specific task.
sentences.zh: 自我效能则是你对自己在某项具体任务上的能力所持有的具体信念。

sentences.en: For example, someone may have high self-efficacy when driving a car, very confident in their driving ability, but they have low self-efficacy when speaking in public.
sentences.zh: 例如，某人在开车时可能具有很高的自我效能，对自己的驾驶能力非常自信，但他们在公开演讲时的自我效能感就很低。

sentences.en: They’re not confident while speaking. What makes Bandura’s work relevant, especially for this episode right now, is his explanation of how self-efficacy develops.
sentences.zh: 他们在讲话时并不自信。使班杜拉的工作具有现实意义的，尤其是对本期节目而言，是他对自我效能是如何发展而来的解释。

sentences.en: He argued that the most powerful source of confidence is “successful experiences.” Confidence grows when we repeatedly prove to ourselves that we can do something.
sentences.zh: 他认为，自信的最强大来源是“成功的经历”。当我们一次次向自己证明我们能够做成某事时，自信就会增长。

sentences.en: I strongly believe in this concept. If you start speaking in English now, you will become more confident over time.
sentences.zh: 我坚信这个概念。如果你现在就开始说英语，随着时间的推移，你会变得更自信。

sentences.en: Bandura described four different sources of self-efficacy, four ways you can build your self-efficacy.
sentences.zh: 班杜拉描述了自我效能的四个不同来源，即你可以建立自我效能的四种方式。

sentences.en: First is “mastery experiences”. Basically, successfully doing the task, repeatedly doing it successfully.
sentences.zh: 首先是“精通经验”。基本上就是成功完成任务，重复地成功完成它。

sentences.en: That builds your confidence. Second is vicarious experiences.
sentences.zh: 这能建立你的自信。其次是替代性经验。

sentences.en: This means seeing people in similar situations being successful or successfully doing something.
sentences.zh: 这意味着看到处境相似的人获得成功或成功完成某事。

sentences.en: That also improves your confidence. Third is social persuasion, so being given positive and credible feedback, like when someone says your English is good and they really mean it.
sentences.zh: 这也能提高你的自信。第三是社会说服，也就是获得积极且可信的反馈，比如当某人说你的英语很好并且是真心实意时。

sentences.en: And finally is your emotional and physiological state.
sentences.zh: 最后是你的情绪和生理状态。

sentences.en: If you can reduce your stress, reduce your anxiety, have a good night’s sleep so you feel less tired, you’ll become more confident.
sentences.zh: 如果你能减轻压力、减少焦虑、美美地睡上一觉从而感觉不那么疲惫，你就会变得更自信。

sentences.en: If we apply these steps to being a confident English speaker.
sentences.zh: 如果我们把这些步骤应用到成为一个自信的英语说者上。

sentences.en: First, speak English repeatedly. The more times you speak, the more times you’re successful.
sentences.zh: 首先，重复地说英语。你开口说的次数越多，成功的次数就越多。

sentences.en: That means the more self-efficacy you will have in English speaking, the more confidence.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你在英语口语方面的自我效能就会越高，自信心也就越强。

sentences.en: You could join my conversation clubs, go to a language exchange meeting, find a speaking partner.
sentences.zh: 你可以加入我的英语角俱乐部，去参加语言交流会，或者找个语伴。

sentences.en: Once you start speaking, you will notice improvements.
sentences.zh: 一旦你开始说话，你就会注意到进步。

sentences.en: Second, see other people like yourself being successful, speaking in English.
sentences.zh: 其次，看到像你一样的人获得成功、用英语说话。

sentences.en: Maybe watch some YouTube videos or TikTok videos of people from your country speaking in English.
sentences.zh: 也许可以看一些来自你国家的YouTube视频或TikTok视频，看看他们是如何用英语说话的。

sentences.en: Third, find an English teacher or someone to give positive feedback when you do well.
sentences.zh: 第三，找一位英语老师或某人在你表现好时给予积极的反馈。

sentences.en: It could be your friend or a teacher. So overall, if you want to be a more confident English speaker, you need to start speaking regularly.
sentences.zh: 这可以是你的朋友或老师。总而言之，如果你想成为一个更自信的英语说者，你需要开始定期开口说话。

sentences.en: After everything we’ve discussed today, I don’t think confidence means being perfect or having perfect grammar or having a native-like accent.
sentences.zh: 在我们今天讨论了这么多之后，我认为自信并不意味着完美无缺、拥有完美的语法或带有母语般的口音。

sentences.en: Confidence is trusting your ability to communicate.
sentences.zh: 自信就是相信自己有能力进行沟通。

sentences.en: It’s believing that you can handle mistakes and difficult situations.
sentences.zh: 它是相信自己能够应付错误和困难的局面。

sentences.en: Many learners tell themselves they are going to start speaking English when they feel more confident, but that’s the wrong way round.
sentences.zh: 许多学习者告诉自己，他们要等到感觉更自信时才开始说英语，但这是本末倒置的。

sentences.en: Confidence comes after action, not before it.
sentences.zh: 自信来自于行动，而不是在行动之前。

sentences.en: Confidence comes from speaking. The more you speak, the more experience.
sentences.zh: 自信源于开口。你说的越多，经验就越多。

sentences.en: The more experience you have, the more evidence you get that you can do it successfully.
sentences.zh: 你的经验越多，你能够成功做到这一点的证据就越多。

sentences.en: And over time, the evidence that you can communicate successfully becomes confidence.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，你能成功沟通的证据就转化成了自信。

sentences.en: But what do you think? Are you a confident English speaker?
sentences.zh: 但你怎么看？你是一个自信的英语说者吗？
